sections.h2: Your selling options in Vernon Hills
sections.html:
A listing agent, a do-it-yourself sale and an as-is cash purchase are the three routes in Vernon Hills. Whichever you pick, the timeline depends mostly on the contract, the title work and any repairs you choose to make.

Vernon Hills is a Lake County village of about 7.95 square miles, split between Libertyville and Vernon townships. Population was 26,850 in 2020 and is estimated at 26,825 for July 2025, so the village has held steady for several years.

Owners occupy 67.5% of homes, and the middle value of an owned home is $412,300. The middle rent with utilities is $1,903 a month. The village has 11,022 households of about 2.43 people, with a midpoint household income of $121,943 and an average commute of 26.9 minutes.

Many residents were born abroad (33.6%), and 41.7% speak another language at home. Buyers often arrive by Metra: the village has a station on the North Central Service, with weekday rush-hour trains between Antioch and Chicago Union Station, and Pace buses also serve it. Mention the train and the school district named on the tax bill when you describe the house, since the Hawthorn district, Vernon Hills High School and Libertyville High School all serve parts of the village.

sections.h2: Repairs that need a village permit
sections.html:
The Community Development Department issues building permits and inspects the work, and its permit page sets out the basics. Doing repairs before a sale is optional, but any permitted work you start should be inspected and closed out so the buyer inherits no open permit.

Vernon Hills residential permit basics
Permit topicRequirement
Review timeTypically 15 business days for residential projects
Quick permitsWater heater, HVAC, roof, siding and sewer repair carry no plan review, released immediately subject to staff availability
PaymentCash or check only
Trade credentialsRequired for electricians, roofers and plumbers; the village does not register contractors
Completion bondRequired for most permit types and refunded after final inspections
InspectionsCall (847) 367-3700 at least one day in advance, before 3:00 p.m.

Applicants should use the current building codes even where a form still shows the 2018 edition. New residential units and substantial renovations also fall under the Electric Vehicle Charging Act, which matters to a buyer who plans to rebuild.

The Community Development Department answers complaints about property maintenance and building code. Complaints go through the village's online service request system or by calling (847) 367-3700.

  • Tall grass and weeds
  • Debris left in the street
  • Work done without a permit
  • Sign code violations

Most vehicle complaints belong with the Police Department.

The department also issues certificates of occupancy for newly occupied units and runs property maintenance inspections, and the permit page links a certificate of occupancy checklist and a pre-inspection checklist. If you are unsure whether a past deck, fence or basement finish was permitted, ask the department before listing, because a buyer's title or lender review can raise the same question.

sections.h2: How the property tax bill is set and paid
sections.html:
Lake County sets Vernon Hills bills on a two-year cycle, so the bill you receive reflects an assessment made the year before. The county's Tax Extension Process page explains the steps: township assessors value each home as of January 1 at one-third of fair market value, the Chief County Assessor equalizes the values, and a blue assessment notice goes out in the fall. Owners then have only 30 days to appeal to the Board of Review. By the time the bill arrives it is too late to contest it.

Bills are mailed each May 1, with the first installment due in early June and the second in early September. Penalty interest of 1.5% is added the day after each due date, and more accrues in later months. A tax sale of delinquent parcels follows in November.

Taxes for the year in progress are usually adjusted between buyer and seller at closing, so get a paid-to-date figure from the Lake County Treasurer before the closing is scheduled.

sections.h2: Appealing an assessment before you sell
sections.html:
The blue assessment notice that arrives in the fall is your one chance each year to contest the value. Read it when it comes, compare it with what similar homes nearby have sold for, and decide quickly, since the window to file with the Board of Review is only 30 days.

A lower assessment helps whoever owns the house next, and buyers notice tax bills when they run their monthly numbers. If you plan to sell within the year, filing on time can make the property easier to market. Keep a copy of the notice and any evidence you send, and pass the paperwork to the buyer's side if the appeal is still open at closing.

sections.h2: Deeds and transfer tax in Lake County
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office in Waukegan. The county's deed packet requires a notarized grantor signature, the grantee's address, a legal description, the preparer's name and a completed PTAX-203 form or an exemption statement. It also lists six municipalities that require a local transfer stamp before recording. Vernon Hills is not among them, but ask the village clerk if your deed has unusual features.

Under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, the state tax is collected through revenue stamps or an electronic indicator. Any sale also has to be reported to the Department of Revenue electronically. Your title company normally handles both, so ask for the figures before closing day.

sections.h2: Before you list or accept a cash offer
sections.html:
Gather your latest tax bill, any permit paperwork for decks, fences or basement finishes, and a payoff figure from your lender. Check with Community Development at (847) 367-3700 about any permit left open, since a buyer's title review can turn it up.

A cash purchase skips the buyer's loan approval and the appraisal that comes with it. The work that remains is the title search, payoff letters, the deed and the PTAX-203. If those are in order, closing can come quickly, and you choose the date together with the buyer. Compare any offer against what a listing would net after repairs, showings and the wait.

At closing you sign the deed, the lender is paid off from your proceeds, and the county records the transfer. Keep copies of everything you sign, and ask the title company to confirm in writing that the old mortgage is released.

faqs.q: Does the village of Vernon Hills inspect a house before a sale?
faqs.a: The village's permit and Community Development pages cover permits, code enforcement and certificates of occupancy for newly occupied units, and none describes a seller inspection tied to a resale. Ask Community Development at (847) 367-3700 if you have open permits or an unusual use.

faqs.q: How long does a Vernon Hills permit review last?
faqs.a: Residential permit applications typically take 15 business days to process. Minor permits such as a water heater, HVAC, roof, siding or sewer repair are released immediately, subject to staff availability.

faqs.q: Does a Vernon Hills sale carry a village transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Lake County deed packet lists six municipalities that require a stamp, and Vernon Hills is not one of them. State and county transfer taxes are collected at recording, so ask your title company for the figures on your deed.

faqs.q: What dates apply to Vernon Hills property tax installments?
faqs.a: Lake County splits the bill in two, due in early June and early September. Bills are mailed at the start of May each year.

faqs.q: Can a cash buyer close fast on a Vernon Hills house?
faqs.a: Yes, when the title is clear and the deed and PTAX-203 are ready for Lake County recording. A cash closing then depends on the title search, payoff letters and the buyer's funds.
